alignments.note: Anarthrous noun; the supplied indefinite determiner is a rule 7 helper on the noun (rule 51's anarthrous clause). The ASV's margin offers *an instructor*, but the text reads *corrector*.
Substantival adjective with no Greek article; under rule 58 it is the nominal word and takes the supplied determiner itself, the case preposition *of* riding along under rule 21.
Anarthrous noun with supplied indefinite determiner as a rule 7 helper.
Anarthrous genitive noun; *of* realizes the case and stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Participle rendered by a bare English participle.
Preposition realized by *in*; the phrase is fronted in the ASV ahead of the noun phrase it modifies.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19; the governed noun stands bare.
Accusative-of-place noun rendered by the bare noun.
Article governing an expressed noun, realized by *the* under rule 19.
Noun rendered by *form*; its determiner stands on the article in front of it.

The ASV writes *of knowledge* with no determiner, so no English *the* stands for this article to anchor; it is unrepresented under rule 23 and the case preposition stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Genitive noun with the case preposition *of* riding on the noun, its article being unrepresented.

Here the ASV does write a determiner, so the article takes *the* with the case preposition *of* riding along under rule 21, headed on *the*. Rule 24: the two genitives of this verse are rendered differently by the ASV, and each is analysed by what the ASV wrote for it. The repeated *of* is a rule 7 helper on the member it introduces under rule 103, not `added`.
Noun rendered by *truth*, bare, its determiner and case preposition standing on the article.

review_notes: All 15 source and 21 target ids partitioned exactly once.

The two parallel genitives τῆς γνώσεως and τῆς ἀληθείας are treated differently only because the ASV writes *of knowledge* and *of the truth*; rule 21 makes the presence of an English determiner the test, and rule 24 requires the same analysis be applied to both, which it is.
